title: Concerning Fire.

68. Concerning the Fire. 68
Once again he said: 'The Fire that burns and is manifested forth to-
day in the cosmos performs five works.
The first work that it performs is this: it releases
and burns the wood and every thing that they set upon it.
The second: it separates forth four likenesses out of the wood, which
are these: the fire and the light, the smoke and the va-
-por.
The third: it gives a taste and a savor to
what they shall cook in it. It also gives a salt and a sweet-
ness to whoever shall touch it. The fourth work which {3}
it performs is this: all the artisans mold through it the
vessels which they shall establish through it.
The fifth: {4}-
it habitually manifests forth a light, that men may see by means of {5}
